pages.lesson:
LESSON: READING FOR INFORMATION: VISUALS

Grade: Grade 9
Subject: ARABIC
Strand: Reading 2.3 Reading for Comprehension (2 sessions) • Reading pace • Comprehensio
Topic 2.8: Reading for Information: Visuals

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Reading for Information: Visuals. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: Why is it good to make plans before carrying out an activity?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. identify vocabulary from a text for comprehension

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: READING FOR INFORMATION: VISUALS
Subject: ARABIC · Grade: Grade 9
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Reading for Information: Visuals helps you succeed in ARABIC. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

KEY FACTS: READING FOR INFORMATION: VISUALS
Language skills grow by daily practice: listen carefully, speak clearly, read every day, write neatly.
Model → guided practice → independent practice.
Always use complete sentences when writing answers.

PART 1: Identify vocabulary from a text for comprehension

What this means
In this part you learn to identify vocabulary from a text for comprehension. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: identify vocabulary from a text for comprehension.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model reading: Read a short paragraph about “Reading for Information: Visuals”, then retell it in 3 sentences.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can identify vocabulary from a text for comprehension. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Reading for Information: Visuals is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Read a short paragraph about “Reading for Information: Visuals”, then retell it in 3 sentences. (skill: identify vocabulary from a text for comprehension)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Reading for Information: Visuals to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: identify vocabulary from a text for comprehension.
3. Make one local Kenya example of Reading for Information: Visuals from your county, market, farm, or school.
4. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Reading for Information: Visuals: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 9 learner study Reading for Information: Visuals?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. Why is it good to make plans before carrying out an activity?
2. How can we find the meaning of new words in a text?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Reading for Information: Visuals means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: identify vocabulary from a text for comprehension.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
